name: Ragda Pattice
subtitle: potato patties drowned in a thin white pea curry with chutneys on top
prepNotes: The ragda should be thin enough to pour, not a thick curry. It is a sauce for the pattice, not a dal.
Crush a ladle of the cooked peas against the pan to thicken it rather than adding flour.

steps.text: Pressure cook the soaked peas with turmeric and salt for 5 whistles until completely soft.
Temper cumin in oil, add ginger and chilli, then tip in the peas with their liquid.
Crush a ladleful against the side of the pan and simmer 10 minutes to a pouring consistency.
steps.tip: Pouring, not spooning. Add hot water if it tightens.

steps.text: Mix the grated potato with cornflour, chaat masala and salt, and shape into 8 patties.
Shallow-fry the pattice on a tawa, 5 minutes a side, until a hard crust forms.
Put two pattice in each bowl and ladle the hot ragda over them.
Top with chopped onion, both chutneys, chaat masala and coriander.

storage: The ragda keeps 3 days refrigerated and thickens; loosen with hot water. Pattice are best fresh but the raw shaped patties keep 2 days.
